---
title: "Install"
---

## Requirements

EvoDAG needs Python 3.11 or newer and [NumPy](https://numpy.org). Those are the only runtime dependencies; scikit-learn is optional (see [Optional packages](#optional-packages)). Part of the library is written in Cython, so a compiled extension is shipped with it; the packaging files of the repository declare Python 3.11, 3.12, 3.13, 3.14 and 3.15 as the versions that are built and tested, on Linux, macOS and Windows.

## From PyPI

```bash
pip install EvoDAG
```

To use the scikit-learn classes of EvoDAG (`EvoDAGClassifier`, `EnsembleClassifier` and their regression counterparts, see [Python](python.qmd)), install the `sklearn` extra, which adds scikit-learn 1.6 or newer:

```bash
pip install 'EvoDAG[sklearn]'
```

When a prebuilt wheel exists for your platform and Python version, `pip` installs it and nothing is compiled. Otherwise `pip` downloads the source distribution and builds it, and then you need what is listed below under [Building from source](#building-from-source).

## From conda-forge

```bash
conda config --add channels conda-forge
conda config --set channel_priority strict
conda install evodag
```

or, with `mamba`:

```bash
mamba install evodag
```

## Building from source

Building the extensions requires a C compiler, Cython 3 or newer and NumPy 2 or newer. Those build requirements are declared in `pyproject.toml`, so a plain `pip install` of a checkout fetches Cython and NumPy by itself; the compiler is the only thing you must provide (`gcc` or `clang` on Linux and macOS, the Microsoft C++ build tools on Windows).

```bash
git clone https://github.com/mgraffg/EvoDAG.git
cd EvoDAG
pip install .
```

For development, install in editable mode and rebuild the extensions after changing a `.pyx` file:

```bash
pip install -e ".[test]"   # the test extra includes scikit-learn
python setup.py build_ext --inplace
python -m pytest -q tests
```

## Check the installation

```bash
python -c "import EvoDAG; print(EvoDAG.__version__)"
EvoDAG-train --version
```

The second command also confirms that the four console scripts (`EvoDAG-params`, `EvoDAG-train`, `EvoDAG-predict` and `EvoDAG-utils`) are on your `PATH`; they are described in the [Command line](cli.qmd) page.

## Optional packages

scikit-learn (`pip install 'EvoDAG[sklearn]'`) enables the scikit-learn classes `EvoDAGClassifier`, `EvoDAGRegressor`, `EnsembleClassifier` and `EnsembleRegressor`. Without it `import EvoDAG` works and so do `EvoDAGE`, the engine and the command line; only `from EvoDAG import EvoDAGClassifier` (and the other three names) raises an `ImportError` that tells you what to install.

`tqdm` is used, when it is installed, to show a progress bar while an ensemble is trained or evaluated. Graphviz is only needed if you want to turn the graph that `Model.graphviz` writes into a picture (see [Native API](native-api.qmd)).
